verses.text: Rehoboam went to Shechem, where all Israel had gathered to make him king.
Jeroboam son of Nebat heard about it while he was still living in Egypt, where he'd fled from King Solomon.
The people sent for him. Jeroboam and the whole assembly of Israel came to Rehoboam and said,
“Your father put a heavy yoke on us. Lighten the burden he placed on us and the hard labor he demanded, and we'll serve you.”
He told them, “Go away for three days, then come back to me.” So the people left.
King Rehoboam consulted the elders who had served his father Solomon while he was alive. “How do you advise me to answer these people?” he asked.
They replied, “Serve these people today and give them a kind answer. If you take care of them now, they'll serve you always.”
But Rehoboam rejected the elders' advice and consulted the young men who had grown up with him and now served him.
He asked them, “How do you think we should answer these people who told me, ‘Lighten the yoke your father put on us’?”
The young men who had grown up with him replied, “Here's what to tell the people who want you to lighten the heavy yoke your father put on them: ‘My little finger is thicker than my father's waist.
My father put a heavy yoke on you. I'll make it heavier. My father disciplined you with whips, and I'll discipline you with scorpions.’”
Jeroboam and all the people came back to Rehoboam on the third day, just as the king had told them to.
The king answered them harshly. He set aside the advice the elders had given him
and followed the younger men's advice. “My father made your yoke heavy,” he said. “I'll make it heavier. My father disciplined you with whips, and I'll discipline you with scorpions.”
The king refused to listen to the people. The LORD had brought this about to fulfill what he'd told Jeroboam son of Nebat through Ahijah from Shiloh.

When all Israel saw that the king wouldn't listen, they answered, “What share do we have in David? We have no inheritance in Jesse's son. Back to your tents, Israel! Look after your own house now, David.” Then the Israelites went home.
Rehoboam still ruled over the Israelites who lived in the towns of Judah.
King Rehoboam sent Adoram, who supervised forced labor, but all Israel stoned him to death. The king scrambled into his chariot and escaped to Jerusalem.
Israel has remained in rebellion against David's house to this day.
When all Israel heard Jeroboam was back, they called him to the assembly and made him king over Israel. Only the tribe of Judah stayed loyal to David's house.
When Rehoboam got to Jerusalem, he gathered Judah and Benjamin, a hundred and eighty thousand chosen warriors, to fight Israel and restore the kingdom to himself, Solomon's son.
But God gave this message to Shemaiah, the man of God:
“Tell Rehoboam son of Solomon, king of Judah, and all the people of Judah and Benjamin and the rest of the people,
‘This is what the LORD says: Don't go up to fight your fellow Israelites. Everyone go home, because this came from me.’” They listened to the LORD and went home, as he'd told them.
Jeroboam built up Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim and lived there. From there he went out and built up Penuel.
Jeroboam thought to himself, “The kingdom could go back to David's family now.
If these people go up to offer sacrifices at the LORD's house in Jerusalem, they'll give their loyalty back to their lord, King Rehoboam of Judah. They'll kill me and go back to Rehoboam.”
So the king took advice and made two gold calves. He told the people, “It's too much for you to keep going up to Jerusalem. Here are your gods, Israel, who brought you out of Egypt!”
He set one calf in Bethel and the other in Dan.
This led the people into sin. They went as far as Dan to worship before the calf there.
Jeroboam built shrines at the high places and appointed priests from among the people, even though they weren't descendants of Levi.

Jeroboam established a festival on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, like the one in Judah. He went up to the altar at Bethel and sacrificed to the calves he'd made. He placed the priests he'd appointed for the high places in Bethel.
On the fifteenth day of the eighth month, a date Jeroboam had picked himself, he went up to the altar he'd built in Bethel. He established a festival for Israel and went to the altar to burn incense.
